title: Conduct, Ethics and Customer Outcomes
summary: An eight-module foundation programme helping all staff make sound ethical judgements, deliver good customer outcomes and speak up when something is wrong.
intro: This training programme equips all staff in a regulated firm to make sound ethical judgements, deliver good outcomes for customers, manage conflicts of interest and speak up when something does not look right.

sections.Aim and Purpose: To give staff at every level a practical understanding of what good conduct looks like in their own role and why it matters to customers, colleagues and the firm. Participants leave able to recognise ethical dilemmas, put customers' interests first and raise concerns with confidence.
sections.What It Covers: Culture and ethics, ethical decision-making, conflicts of interest, treating customers fairly and good outcomes, clear communication, customers in vulnerable circumstances, complaints, and speaking up, whistleblowing and personal accountability.
Intended Audience: All staff in regulated firms, from new joiners to experienced colleagues, as induction or annual refresher training
Customer-facing, product, marketing, operations, technology and support staff whose work affects customer outcomes
Team leaders and managers who set the tone for conduct and respond when concerns are raised
Learning Objectives: Explain what good conduct and a healthy culture look like in a regulated firm
Apply ethical judgement to everyday dilemmas and grey areas
Identify and manage conflicts of interest in their own work
Deliver fair treatment and good outcomes for customers, including those in vulnerable circumstances
Recognise, handle and learn from complaints
Speak up, escalate concerns and take personal accountability for their own conduct
sections.Structure and Format: Eight modules of about ninety minutes each, delivered in person, virtually or in a hybrid format, either as a two-day programme or as a series of short live sessions, and well suited to conversion into e-learning. Modules combine short briefings with real-world examples and scenario questions, work well as annual refresher training, and can be selected or tailored to the firm's policies and business.
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: No prior knowledge of regulation is required. Some experience of working with customers is helpful but not essential.
Core Reading: FSB (2018), Strengthening Governance Frameworks to Mitigate Misconduct Risk: A Toolkit for Firms and Supervisors
G20/OECD (2022), High-Level Principles on Financial Consumer Protection
FSB (2014), Guidance on Supervisory Interaction with Financial Institutions on Risk Culture: A Framework for Assessing Risk Culture
ISO (2021), ISO 37002:2021 Whistleblowing Management Systems – Guidelines

modules.title: Culture, Ethics and Why Conduct Matters
modules.summary: What culture and conduct mean in a regulated firm, why supervisors care about them, and how everyday behaviour shapes outcomes for customers and markets.
objectives: Explain the link between culture, conduct and customer and market outcomes
Recognise the signs of healthy and unhealthy cultures
Describe what supervisors and customers expect of firms and their staff
syllabus: Conduct risk in plain terms: how harm happens
Culture: tone from the top, the middle and within teams
Lessons from major conduct failures across the industry
Seeing your firm the way a supervisor does

modules.title: Ethical Decision-Making in Practice
modules.summary: Practical tools for working through ethical dilemmas and grey areas, including the pressures, incentives and biases that lead good people to make poor decisions.
objectives: Apply a simple ethical decision-making framework to workplace dilemmas
Recognise how targets, incentives and pressure can distort judgement
Distinguish what is permitted from what is right
syllabus: Ethical tests: fairness, transparency and the headline test
Pressure, incentives and rationalisation
Behavioural biases: groupthink, deference and normalisation of deviance
Dilemma exercise: when the rules do not give a clear answer

modules.title: Conflicts of Interest in Everyday Work
modules.summary: How conflicts of interest arise between the firm, its staff and its customers, and the practical steps staff take to identify, record and manage them.
objectives: Identify actual, potential and perceived conflicts of interest
Apply the firm's conflicts policy, including disclosure and recording
Escalate conflicts that cannot be managed at team level
syllabus: Types of conflict: firm and customer, customer and customer, staff and firm
Remuneration, sales incentives and targets
Personal relationships, outside interests and misuse of position
Managing conflicts: avoidance, controls, disclosure and the conflicts register

modules.title: Treating Customers Fairly and Delivering Good Outcomes
modules.summary: What fair treatment and good customer outcomes mean in practice across products, pricing, service and support, and how each role contributes to them.
objectives: Explain the principles of fair treatment and good customer outcomes
Recognise products, practices and sales behaviours that cause foreseeable harm
Describe how the firm monitors and evidences customer outcomes
syllabus: Acting in good faith and avoiding foreseeable harm
Products that meet customers' needs and offer fair value
Customer support, unreasonable friction and sludge practices
Outcome testing, management information and what good looks like

modules.title: Clear Communication and Customer Understanding
modules.summary: How to communicate with customers fairly, clearly and without misleading them, so that they understand what they are buying and can make informed decisions.
objectives: Apply the fair, clear and not misleading standard to written, verbal and digital communications
Recognise misleading framing, omissions and pressure selling
Check customer understanding at key points in the customer journey
syllabus: Fair, clear and not misleading in practice
Risk warnings, fees and charges: balance and prominence
Digital journeys, choice architecture and dark patterns
Testing and evidencing customer understanding

modules.title: Customers in Vulnerable Circumstances
modules.summary: How to recognise customers who may be in vulnerable circumstances, respond with care and flexibility, and record and share information appropriately.
objectives: Recognise the drivers and signs of vulnerability
Respond to vulnerable customers with appropriate support and adjustments
Record and share information sensitively and in line with data protection rules
syllabus: Drivers of vulnerability: health, life events, resilience and capability
Spotting signs in conversations, behaviour and account activity
Practical adjustments, third-party support and powers of attorney
Financial abuse, scams and when to escalate

modules.title: Complaints: Listening, Resolving and Learning
modules.summary: How to recognise a complaint, handle it fairly and promptly, and use complaints as insight into customer harm and its root causes.
objectives: Recognise expressions of dissatisfaction that amount to a complaint
Handle complaints fairly, promptly and with empathy
Explain how root cause analysis turns complaints into improvements
syllabus: What counts as a complaint, however and wherever it is expressed
Handling and resolving complaints: timeliness, fairness and redress
Referral to the external dispute resolution body
Root cause analysis and learning from complaints

modules.title: Speaking Up, Whistleblowing and Personal Accountability
modules.summary: Why speaking up protects customers, colleagues and the firm, the channels and protections available, and the conduct standards each individual is accountable for, closing with practical scenarios.
objectives: Explain the conduct standards and personal accountability that apply to all staff
Use internal and external channels for raising concerns, including whistleblowing
Apply the programme to realistic workplace dilemmas
syllabus: Individual conduct standards, fitness and propriety and the consequences of misconduct
Psychological safety and the cost of silence
Whistleblowing channels, confidentiality and protection from detriment
Workshop: what would you do? Conduct and customer dilemmas

related.title: Market Conduct Essentials: Inside Information, Conflicts and Personal Dealing
related.summary: A six-module foundation programme helping all staff handle inside information, personal dealing, gifts and communications correctly and avoid market abuse.

related.title: Regulatory Essentials for All Staff
related.summary: An eight-module foundation programme giving all staff a practical understanding of regulation, conduct, financial crime awareness and their own responsibilities.

related.title: AI for Financial Services Professionals
related.summary: A six-module foundation programme giving staff the practical skills to use generative AI productively and safely, in line with the firm's AI policy.

related.title: Cyber, Data and Resilience Essentials
related.summary: A six-module foundation programme giving all staff the practical habits to resist cyber attacks, protect data, use AI tools safely and report incidents.

related.title: Financial Crime Essentials for All Staff
related.summary: An eight-module foundation programme helping all staff recognise financial crime red flags, follow the firm's controls and report suspicions without tipping off.

related.title: Sustainable Finance Essentials
related.summary: A six-module foundation programme giving all staff a practical grounding in ESG, climate risk, sustainable products and avoiding greenwashing.
